chunks.label: Ways to get around
chunks.rationale: Say how you get somewhere: by train, bus, bike or taxi.
chunks.interference: Basu (bus) also turns up as bath in loanwords like basutaoru.

chunks.label: Paying at the till
chunks.rationale: Handle the checkout: card or cash, change, receipt.
chunks.interference: Reshiito is the till slip, not the formal ryoushuusho receipt.

chunks.label: Shopping and prices
chunks.rationale: Talk about going shopping, what things cost and getting them cheaper.
chunks.interference: Seeru is a sale event, waribiki is a discount on an item.

chunks.label: Messages and online
chunks.rationale: Talk about emailing, messaging and doing things online.
chunks.interference: Meeru is often any phone message, not only email.

chunks.label: Hobbies and shows
chunks.rationale: Talk about what you like doing and watching.
chunks.interference: Dorama is a scripted series; bangumi is any show on TV.

chunks.label: Out and back home
chunks.rationale: Talk about heading out, getting home and being picked up.

chunks.label: Trips away
chunks.rationale: Plan a trip: bags, souvenirs, hot springs.
chunks.interference: Ryokou is an ordinary trip; tabi is a more emotional journey.

chunks.label: Dates and nights out
chunks.rationale: Make plans for dates, drinks and parties.
chunks.interference: A paatii is a planned party; drinks with coworkers is a nomikai.

chunks.label: Free and extras
chunks.rationale: Say something costs nothing or comes as a bonus.
chunks.interference: Tada is casual, muryou is what signs say; saabisu often means free, not service.

chunks.label: Booking, ordering, paying
chunks.rationale: Book a table, order, pay and split the bill.
chunks.interference: Shiharai is the formal noun; with friends you use harau or warikan.

chunks.label: Sky and scenery
chunks.rationale: Point out the sky, stars, blossoms and a good view.

chunks.label: Nature and animals
chunks.rationale: Talk about the outdoors, rivers and animals.
chunks.interference: Kawa also means skin or leather.

chunks.label: Celebrations and events
chunks.rationale: Talk about celebrating, weddings and events you're going to.
chunks.interference: Oiwai is the celebration or gift; omedetou is what you say.

chunks.label: Traffic and crowds
chunks.rationale: Describe lights, jams and packed trains on the way somewhere.

chunks.label: News and emergencies
chunks.rationale: Talk about the news, earthquakes and urgent situations.

chunks.label: Debt and scams
chunks.rationale: Talk about who's rich, who owes money and who got scammed.

chunks.label: Contracts and paperwork
chunks.rationale: Deal with contracts, personal details and official forms.
chunks.interference: Kojin is individual, not private life (puraibeeto).

drops.reason: Duplicate of お迎え (same word without the polite o-); the bare form is covered in its notes.
